thread:
maria: Heads up — microlatency tile started showing negative 'decode' attribution on /chat-compress after yesterday's kv-prefetch change. Pulled a p95 slice and saw negative values.

raj: Negative decode is a known smell when timers overlap. Do you have the raw query?

maria: Pulled this quick PromQL for a 1m window: 
```
sum by(route) (increase(ttft_kernel_ns_sum{route="/chat-compress"}[1m]))\n- sum by(route) (increase(decode_ns_sum{route="/chat-compress"}[1m]))\n```

maria: Sometimes the result goes < 0 for p95.

oliver: Can you attach a span timeline for a sample trace so we can see ordering of events?

maria: Pasting a compact span timeline from a single request: 
```
0ms: request_received
12ms: kv_prefetch_start
45ms: kv_prefetch_end
48ms: kernel_start
80ms: kernel_end
82ms: decode_start
120ms: decode_end
```

maria: That one looks fine, decode after kernel. But when microbatching, we've seen kv_prefetch_end > kernel_start (prefetch finishes while kernel is still running) and our dashboard derivation treats prefetch and kernel as disjoint which is wrong.

raj: Current dashboard math is naive: decode = total - kernel - prefetch. That double-counts overlaps and can produce negatives. We need an intersection-aware decomposition.

yen: +1. We should stop doing overlap math in Grafana queries. Make exporter emit lightweight event markers, then compute overlaps in an offline reducer.

sam: Concern: extra timers in the hot path can perturb latencies. Suggestion: emit one counter-per-event (kernel_start, kernel_end, prefetch_end etc.) with ns timestamps as labels and keep runtime overhead minimal.

oliver: Counters + offline reducer sounds good. Offline compute avoids runtime aggregation costs. We can generate corrected rollups (kernel_only_ns, decode_only_ns, prefetch_only_ns, kernel_prefetch_overlap_ns) aggregated per route and latency bucket.

maria: Proposed plan:
1) Add event counters and minimal ns tags (route, batch_id, kernel_variant) in the exporter.
2) Nightly reducer job that reads recent traces/events and computes pairwise overlaps, producing rollup gauges (p50/p95/p99) per route and bucket.
3) Update microlatency dashboard to read corrected rollups and show an "overlap_correction" flag on the tile.

raj: Also add a dev note on semantics: p99 shown on the microlatency tile will be the overlap-corrected number. If we keep the old naive query then users will see negative bars. Add callout to explain why.

sam: I'll prototype the reducer in Python using pandas. Rough sketch: 
```
def reduce(events_df):\n    # events_df rows: trace_id, route, event, ts_ns\n    # build intervals per trace and compute pairwise intersection lengths\n    ...\n    return aggregates_by_route\n```
I'll push PoC by EOD.

maria: Good. If PoC looks solid we'll flip dashboard queries to the corrected rollups. Can we also tag by batch_size and kernel_variant so we can correlate kernel choices / quantization to overlap frequency?

yen: Yup add batch_size and kernel_variant labels. Also capture microbatch_id when available.

oliver: Quick operational ask: add an alert that fires if negative decode fraction > 0.01 (1%) across routes. Page eng-runtime on-call. Without correction that could signal a regression.

raj: I'll draft the alert and a Grafana annotation explaining overlap vs naive subtraction.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: perf-instrumentation/event-counters -> canary start 02:12 UTC

maria: Canary watchers please pay attention to /chat-compress and /embed-fast — they showed the largest skew in yesterday's runs.

sam: I'll include unit tests for the reducer covering edge cases: full containment, partial overlap, and simultaneous boundaries.

maria: Thanks team. After reducer lands we'll add a small explainer panel on the microlatency tile so PMs/CS don't freak out at negative bars. :thumbsup:
